input.quote: 15. ASSIGNMENT OR TRANSFER. Neither party shall assign or transfer any of its rights under this Agreement without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
input.rationale: Section 15 is the only assignment provision and there is no change-of-control language anywhere in the Agreement, so TrueLink has no exit or re-pricing right on our change of control (that limb is satisfied). However, the clause fails the fallback on two material terms: (i) it gives Client no carve-out for assignment to a successor in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets — only a "financially responsible affiliate" — so a corporate transaction would require TrueLink's approval; and (ii) approval is at TrueLink's absolute discretion, with no "not unreasonably withheld" standard, which the fallback requires. A prohibition on Client assignment with no M&A carve-out is walk-away territory under the rule. Our redline makes the minimal edit to reach the preferred position: it adds the successor carve-out for Client and a reasonableness standard on consent, leaving the mutual structure and affiliate carve-out intact. We did not press the further preferred sub-elements (an express bar on TrueLink assigning to a Client competitor) given the existing mutual bargain; that is noted rather than flagged.

ops.oldText: without the prior written approval of the other party, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate.
ops.newText: without the prior written approval of the other party, which approval shall not be unreasonably withheld or delayed, except no such approval shall be required for an assignment to a financially responsible affiliate or, in the case of Client, to a successor in a merger, acquisition, reorganization or sale of substantially all of its assets.

proposal.comment: [Playbook] We added the customary successor carve-out so Client can assign in a merger, acquisition or sale of substantially all assets, and made consent subject to a reasonableness standard. Our playbook does not accept an absolute veto over Client's corporate transactions; the affiliate carve-out and mutuality are otherwise unchanged.
proposal.summary: Add successor/M&A assignment carve-out for Client and a not-unreasonably-withheld consent standard.
